sourceFacts.layout: Two columns and three rows; left column a,b,c; right column d,e,f after transliterating the six source Cyrillic subfigure letters in reading-by-column order.

panels.observed: A at left, a convex lens in the middle, two bounding directed rays meeting on the vertical film line at right.
B nearer the lens than A; the bounding outgoing rays are still separated on the film line. No downstream exact-focus point is drawn.
C farther from the lens than A; outgoing bounding rays cross before the film line and are separated again at that line.
Same A distance and lens/film arrangement as a. Four incoming boundary paths; outer paths end at the aperture bars, inner paths continue and meet on the film line.
Same nearer B case as b. Four incoming boundary paths, outer blocked paths and a narrower transmitted bundle; nonzero film-plane separation is visibly smaller than in b.
Same farther C case as c. Outer blocked paths; narrower transmitted paths cross before film and remain separated on it by less than in c.

sharedStructure: Each lens is centrally thick, with an upright outline, end caps and repeated short diagonal interior marks.
Lens-to-film arrangement is unchanged in the repeated cases, allowing a fixed-film comparison in local panel coordinates.
All ray arrowheads point from the left object toward the right film.
Right-column aperture bars are immediately to the RIGHT of the lens in these actual source pixels, with an open central gap.
Each right-column source point repeats the corresponding left-column distance ordering.
The film is shown edge-on as a vertical line. B' and C' label film-plane defocus locations, not exact conjugate image points.
notInPixels: No numerical focal length, object distance, image distance or aperture diameter.
No coordinate axis, scale, dimension labels, diffraction pattern or quantitative aberration.
No geometric proof that an arbitrary finite-angle physical lens has exact concurrence.
sourceFacts.sourceTextTension: The supplied current bilingual prose says the aperture is before the objective. The inspected source places its bars to the right. Keep the source-side position; explicitly declare the image-side-stop thin-lens construction and request independent FIG resolution rather than moving the bars silently.

modernAdditions: Exact selected u/v/f coordinates satisfy the ideal paraxial thin-lens equation. No numerical optical givens are printed.
Lens profiles and diagonal glass marks are regularized source structure, not measured curvatures or counted optical rays.

Image-side stop has a fixed physical half-gap. Its admitted lens height depends on conjugate distance; blocked rays stop at the bars. This preserves the source-side stop without silently claiming it was before the objective.
Thick short film-plane segments represent edge-on defocus diameters, not front-view circles. B-prime/C-prime name film spots and never the hidden exact conjugate points.
Only A is represented by a point on film. Nonzero B/C defocus remains after stopping down; diffraction/aberration are not modeled.
English opening headers and a Paraxial model scope label are deliberate instructional additions.
Directed rays use native segment and polygon objects with connects/on-line assertions; they do not depend on SVG marker geometry.
